prop:unit-modulus-eigenvalue:
Proposition Eigenvalues of even braids on V_{(2,1)} and the Borromean trace. Let \beta be a braid word of even length in H_3(q). On the standard representation \rho_{(2,1)}, \det \rho_{(2,1)}(\beta) = 1, so the two eigenvalues satisfy \lambda_1 \lambda_2 = 1. They lie on the unit circle exactly when \chi_{(2,1)}(\beta) is real with |\chi_{(2,1)}(\beta)| \le 2; this is not automatic. For the Borromean braid \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3,

  \chi_{(2,1)}(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})
  \;=\;
  -\frac{(q^4 - q^2 + 1)(q^8 - 2q^6 - 2q^2 + 1)}{q^6},

which equals 2 at q = 1.
prf:unit-modulus-eigenvalue:
Proof Proof of unit modulus eigenvalue. The Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1 (where h = q - q^{-1}) gives each generator eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} on V_{(2,1)}, with product -1; \sigma_i^{-1} has eigenvalues q^{-1} and -q, also with product -1. For a word of n letters, \det \rho_{(2,1)}(\beta) = (-1)^n, which is 1 for even n. So \lambda_1 \lambda_2 = 1, and the characteristic polynomial is \lambda^2 - \chi\,\lambda + 1. Its roots have modulus 1 if and only if \chi is real with |\chi| \le 2. That condition can fail: \sigma_1^2 has eigenvalues q^2 and q^{-2}.

For the Borromean value, take the explicit model \rho_{(2,1)}(\sigma_1) = \mathrm{diag}(q, -q^{-1}) and

  \rho_{(2,1)}(\sigma_2) =
  \begin{pmatrix}
    -\dfrac{1}{q(q^2+1)} & 1 \\[1ex]
    \dfrac{q^4 + q^2 + 1}{(q^2+1)^2} & \dfrac{q^3}{q^2+1}
  \end{pmatrix},

which satisfies the braid relation, with \sigma_2^{-1} = \sigma_2 - h. Multiplying out (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3 and taking the trace gives the displayed formula. \square
prop:convention-d-kills-antisymmetriser:
Proposition z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is the unique non-trivial Markov trace on H_3(q) whose radical contains the three-strand antisymmetriser. Let

  \mathrm{tr}_M \;=\; y_{(3)}\,\chi^{(3)} \;+\; y_{(2,1)}\,\chi^{(2,1)} \;+\; y_{(1^3)}\,\chi^{(1^3)}

be the Wedderburn expansion of a Markov trace on H_3(q), normalised by \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) = z and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0\sigma_1) = z^2. Then for every q > 0

  \boxed{\;\;
  y_{(1^3)} \;=\; 0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  z \;=\; q
  \;\;\text{ or }\;\;
  z \;=\; \frac{q^{3}}{q^{2}+1},
  \;\;}

and the first root forces y_{(3)} = 1, y_{(2,1)} = y_{(1^3)} = 0. The parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) therefore defines the unique non-trivial Markov trace on H_3(q) whose radical contains the three-strand antisymmetriser.
prf:convention-d-kills-antisymmetriser: Proof Proof: elimination, factorisation, and the exclusion of the trivial branch.
prop:markov-branching-three-term:
Proposition Branching coherence of the Markov trace reduces to [m+2]_q + [m]_q = [2]_q\,[m+1]_q. Let y_{(n-k,k)} = [n-2k+1]_q/[2]_q^{\,n} be the two-row Markov weights at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Then adding a box to a two-row Young diagram is coherent with the trace,

  y_{(n+1-k,\,k)} \;+\; y_{(n-k,\,k+1)} \;=\; y_{(n-k,\,k)},

and this identity is, after clearing [2]_q^{\,n+1}, exactly the three-term recursion

  \boxed{\;\; [m+2]_q \;+\; [m]_q \;=\; [2]_q\,[m+1]_q. \;\;}
rem:hecke-radical-is-temperley-lieb:
Remark The radical is the Temperley--Lieb ideal: \sum \dim^{2} over the surviving blocks is C_n. The Markov trace at z = q^3/(q^2+1) does not annihilate the three-strand antisymmetriser by accident. The row cap propagates up the whole tower, and what it leaves behind is a named algebra.

Because the fundamental representation of SU(2) is two-dimensional, no q-antisymmetriser exists on three of its strands, and the Wedderburn weight of any partition with three or more rows vanishes identically --- not numerically at q_0, but as a rational function of q. The surviving blocks of H_n(q) are therefore exactly the two-row shapes. Summing the squared Specht dimensions over those shapes gives, level by level, the Catalan numbers:

n surviving shapes \sum \dim^{2} \dim H_n(q) C_n
2 (2),\,(1,1) 2 2 2
3 (3),\,(2,1) 5 6 5
4 (4),\,(3,1),\,(2,2) 14 24 14
5 (5),\,(4,1),\,(3,2) 42 120 42
6 (6),\,(5,1),\,(4,2),\,(3,3) 132 720 132
7 (7),\,(6,1),\,(5,2),\,(4,3) 429 5040 429

The quotient of H_n(q) by the radical of its Markov form thus has the dimension of the Temperley--Lieb algebra TL_n(q), and the blocks match shape by shape. At n = 4 the bookkeeping closes exactly: 24 - 14 = 10 = 3^{2} + 1^{2}, the discarded (2,1,1) and (1^{4}) blocks, so the quotient is the direct sum of the three surviving matrix algebras and not a proper quotient of it.
prop:markov-gram-star-positive:
Proposition The Markov--Gram star form is positive semidefinite; positivity reduces to y_\lambda \ge 0. Let T_w^{*} = T_{w^{-1}} be the Hecke star and let

  S_{ij} \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(b_i\,b_j^{*}\bigr)

be the Gram matrix of the Markov trace on the normal-form basis b \in \{\gamma,\, \sigma_0,\, \sigma_1,\, L_+,\, L_-,\, e^{-}\} of H_3(q). Then S is positive semidefinite whenever every Wedderburn weight satisfies y_\lambda \ge 0, and its kernel is spanned by the blocks with y_\lambda = 0.
rem:markov-gram-bilinear-vs-star: Remark Two pairings, two signatures: \mathrm{tr}_M(b_ib_j) versus \mathrm{tr}_M(b_ib_j^{*}). The normal-form basis of H_3(q) admits two Gram matrices, and they do not have the same signature. Which one is meant has to be said.
prop:gram-degeneracy-blocks-connes:
Proposition A Lipschitz seminorm with nonzero kernel has no finite Connes sup. Let L be a Lipschitz seminorm on an algebra of observables, let \varphi and \psi be states, and let

  d(\varphi,\psi) \;=\; \sup\,\bigl\{\, |\varphi(a) - \psi(a)| \;:\; L(a) \le 1 \,\bigr\}

be the associated Connes distance. If some k satisfies L(k) = 0 while \varphi(k) \ne \psi(k), then the supremum is unbounded: for every proposed bound M there is an admissible b with |\varphi(b) - \psi(b)| > M.
cor:finite-connes-forces-trivial-kernel:
Corollary Finite Connes distance forces a trivial kernel --- hence the quotient by the radical. Suppose the Connes supremum is finite: some M bounds |\varphi(b) - \psi(b)| over every b with L(b) \le 1. Then no kernel element of L separates \varphi from \psi --- for every k with L(k) = 0 one has \varphi(k) = \psi(k).

This is the contrapositive of the obstruction, and it is worth stating separately because it converts a negative result into an instruction. Finiteness of the distance is not something one may hope for and then check; it is equivalent to the seminorm having no separating kernel. A construction that wants a finite distance must therefore arrange the kernel away first.

On the Markov--Gram form the arrangement is forced and unique. The kernel is the radical of the pairing, so the only way to satisfy the hypothesis is to pass to the quotient by it. What makes this a restatement rather than an amputation is the identification of the quotient: the radical is the Temperley--Lieb ideal, and H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad} is TL_n(q), an algebra with its own diagrammatic calculus and its own standard form. The instruction "quotient so the distance exists" and the instruction "work in Temperley--Lieb" are the same instruction, and the Catalan count is what identifies them.

On the quotient the star form is positive definite, since the surviving blocks are exactly those with y_\lambda > 0 and each contributes a sum of squares. A definite form is what a Rieffel Lipschitz seminorm needs, so the construction that the degeneracy blocked runs unobstructed one level down.

One qualification travels with the repair. Deleting the radical is observationally free: no trace value moves, because the deleted block already contributed zero.
prop:interface-knot-markov-z:
Proposition Interface-knot contribution to canonical-atom Markov trace equals the Markov parameter z exactly. Let \mathcal{B}_K \in H_{3A}(q) be the canonical atomic braid for atom K. Let \mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}} be the disjoint Hecke product of its constituent nucleons. The interface knot \bowtie_K connects the blocks: \mathcal{B}_K = b_1\,\varepsilon_1\,b_2 \cdots \varepsilon_{A-1}\,b_A, where b_i is the word of the i-th nucleon on its own block of consecutive strands and each \varepsilon_i = \sigma_{g_i}^{\pm 1} is a single generator joining blocks i and i+1.

The Markov trace ratio identically satisfies:

  \boxed{\;
    \frac{\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K)}{\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}})}
    \;=\; z(q)^{p_+(K)} \cdot \bigl(z(q) - h(q)\bigr)^{p_-(K)}
  \;}

where z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1) is the Markov parameter, h(q) is the Hecke skein parameter, and p_+ / p_- count the positive / negative interface generators.

This exact factorisation governs atomic assembly. Adding a proton inserts a positive interface, scaling the trace by z. Adding a neutron after a proton also inserts a positive interface. Adding a neutron to an existing neutron inserts a negative interface, scaling the trace by z-h.

The structural interface identity completely determines the trace scaling. The empirical single-block extraction correction operates independently at a different structural level.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring.
prf:interface-knot-markov-z:
Proof Proof of interface knot markov z. (Markov axiom and Hecke skein.)

For a positive interface generator \sigma_g, the Markov axiom (Existence and non-degeneracy of the Markov trace (Jones, 1987)) gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g) \;=\; z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)
  \qquad \forall\, \alpha \in H_{n}(q).

For a negative interface generator \sigma_g^{-1}, the Hecke skein relation \sigma_g^{-1} = \sigma_g - h \cdot \mathbf{1} combined with linearity of \mathrm{tr}_M gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g^{-1})
  \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha \cdot \sigma_g) - h \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha)
  \;=\; (z - h) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\alpha).

These two identities apply when the interface generator is the last letter. In \mathcal{B}_K an interface generator sits between two blocks, so the iteration needs a block-multiplicativity lemma.

Lemma (block multiplicativity). Let x \in H_{k+1}(q), let y \in H_m(q), and let \mathrm{sh}_{k+1}(y) be y with every \sigma_i replaced by \sigma_{i+k+1}. Then

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,\mathrm{sh}_{k+1}(y)\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(x\,\sigma_k\,\mathrm{sh}_{k+1}(y)\bigr) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y).

Proof. Put a = x or a = x\sigma_k; in both cases a lies in H_{k+2}(q). Consider the linear map y \mapsto \mathrm{tr}_M(a\,\mathrm{sh}_{k+1}(y)). For m = 1 it gives \mathrm{tr}_M(a). For m \ge 2, write a basis element of H_m(q) as T_u\,\sigma_{m-1}\,T_v with u, v \in S_{m-1}, or as T_u with u \in S_{m-1}. In the first case \mathrm{sh}(T_v)\,a\,\mathrm{sh}(T_u) lies in H_{m+k}(q), so cyclicity, the Markov property for the top generator \sigma_{m+k}, and cyclicity again give

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(a\,\mathrm{sh}(T_u)\,\sigma_{m+k}\,\mathrm{sh}(T_v)\bigr)
  = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\mathrm{sh}(T_v)\,a\,\mathrm{sh}(T_u)\bigr)
  = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(a\,\mathrm{sh}(T_u T_v)\bigr).

In the second case \mathrm{sh}(T_u) lies in H_{m+k}(q) and the trace restricts. This is the same recursion that computes \mathrm{tr}_M(y) from \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, so the map equals \mathrm{tr}_M(a)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(y). The Markov property gives \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_k) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x). \square

Now write \mathcal{B}_K = b_1\,\varepsilon_1\,b_2\,\varepsilon_2 \cdots \varepsilon_{A-1}\,b_A, where b_i is the word of the i-th nucleon on its own block of strands and \varepsilon_i = \sigma_{g_i}^{\pm 1} joins blocks i and i+1; the vacuum braid is b_1 b_2 \cdots b_A. Applying the lemma A - 1 times, with \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h for the negative connectors, gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K) = z^{p_+}(z-h)^{p_-} \prod_i \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i), and \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}}) = \prod_i \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i). Dividing yields the boxed identity (\star). An exact check over \mathbb{Q} at q = 2 (three blocks on nine strands, one positive and one negative connector) reproduces z(z-h).
conj:block-multiplicativity-v-free:
Conjecture Block-multiplicativity of per-generator \hat{V} on the disjoint Hecke product. Let \mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}} = \mathcal{B}_p^{(1)} \cdots \mathcal{B}_n^{(N)} \in H_{3A}(q) denote the constituent vacuum—the disjoint Hecke product of Z proton braids and N neutron braids on disjoint 3-strand blocks, with no interface crossings. For each generator \sigma_g acting only inside the k-th nucleon block, the Wedderburn-weighted per-generator character ratio

  \hat V^{(3A)}_g(\mathcal{B}_K^{\mathrm{vac}})
   :=
  \sum_{\lambda \vdash 3A}
    \frac{\dim_q^2(\lambda)}{[3A]_q!} \cdot
    \frac{\chi^\lambda(W_g)}{\dim(\lambda)}

is independent of A. It depends only on the flavor of the k-th nucleon and on the local position g \bmod 3 \in \{0, 1\} within the block, not on the total strand count 3A or the flavor content of the other blocks.
prop:lusztig-vs-hermitian-bar:
Proposition Lusztig bar (q \mapsto q^{-1}) vs Hermitian-\ast (q \mapsto \overline{q}^{-1}) on the complex Hecke algebra: the two anti-involutions coincide on the parameter iff q \in \mathbb{R}. On the unit circle |q| = 1, Lusztig coincides with complex conjugation (\overline{q} = q^{-1}) while Hermitian becomes the identity on q; on general |q| > 1 with \mathrm{Im}(q) \neq 0 the three involutions (Lusztig, Hermitian, complex conjugation) are pairwise distinct. The split is the categorical home for any future \mathrm{Im}(q_0) contribution. On the complex Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(\mathbb{C}, q) with q \in \mathbb{C}^\times, the two ring anti-involutions

\beta_L \colon q \mapsto q^{-1},\quad \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}
\qquad\text{(Lusztig bar)},
\beta_H \colon q \mapsto \overline{q}^{\,-1},\quad \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}
\qquad\text{(Hermitian \(\ast\))}

coincide on the parameter q if and only if \mathrm{Im}(q) = 0, equivalently q \in \mathbb{R}.
prf:lusztig-vs-hermitian-bar:
Proof Proof of lusztig vs hermitian bar. The two involutions act identically on the braid generators \sigma_i (both send \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}), so the question reduces to the parameter action. Then \beta_L(q) = q^{-1} and \beta_H(q) = \overline{q}^{\,-1}. For q \in \mathbb{C}^\times,

q^{-1} \;=\; \overline{q}^{\,-1} \;\iff\; q \;=\; \overline{q} \;\iff\; \mathrm{Im}(q) = 0. \quad\square
prop:q-zero-complex-extension:
Proposition The pre-Archimedean substrate is polymorphic in its base ring: specializing to R = \mathbb{C} with |q| > 1 is admissible without modifying the Hecke quadratic, the bar involution, the Frobenius pairing, or the Markov trace. The current real-axis convention q_0 \in \mathbb{R}, q_0 > 1 is one such specialization; complex q_0 with |q_0| > 1 and \mathrm{Im}(q_0) \neq 0 is uninstantiated infrastructure. Let R be a commutative ring and q \in R^\times a unit. Every pre-Archimedean substrate identity—the Hecke quadratic

  \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1,

the bar involution q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}, \sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1}, the Frobenius pairing \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_F, and the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M—is stated polymorphically in R. The specialization R = \mathbb{C} with q_0 \in \mathbb{C} and \lvert q_0 \rvert > 1 is admissible. The substrate identities transfer verbatim, with \lvert q \rvert > 1 replacing the archimedean ordering q > 1 as the substrate-level non-degeneracy condition.
prf:q-zero-complex-extension:
Proof Proof of q zero complex extension. Each substrate identity is stated in the cited literature (Wenzl 1988; Jones 1987) over a commutative ring with q a unit; the substrate identities used here (the bi-filtration of H_q, the explicit central idempotent, the categorical q-Lie bracket and the bar involution) are likewise stated over a commutative ring R (or a stronger structure) with q \in R and without any ordering predicate on q.

The condition \lvert q \rvert > 1 on \mathbb{C} is sufficient to make q a unit (since \lvert q \rvert > 0 implies q \neq 0), so the existing polymorphic identities specialize. \quad\square
prop:cellular-depth-filtration:
Proposition Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)): GB-depth as Lusztig's a-function, a filtration by ideals that the Goldman involution carries to the n(\lambda)-filtration; conditional parity transfer. Let K be a field and q\in K^\times such that H_n=H_n(K,q) is split semisimple, let \{e_\lambda\}_{\lambda\vdash n} be its central primitive idempotents, and let Z=Z(H_n). For a function \delta from partitions of n to \mathbb N, the cellular \delta-filtration of Z is

F^\delta_k := \operatorname{span}_K\{e_\lambda : \delta(\lambda)\le k\},\qquad k\in\mathbb N.

The GB-depth of \lambda is Lusztig's a-function of the two-sided Kazhdan–Lusztig cell of shape \lambda, which in the labelling where (n) is the index representation is

a(\lambda)=\sum_i\binom{\lambda_i}{2}.

Write n(\lambda)=\sum_i(i-1)\lambda_i, so that a(\lambda')=n(\lambda). Let \# be the Goldman involution \sigma_i\mapsto-\sigma_i^{-1}, which satisfies \#(e_\lambda)=e_{\lambda'} (Schur-Weyl justification of shell-operator self-duality). Then:

  1. (Filtration by ideals.) For every \delta: F^\delta_j\subseteq F^\delta_k for j\le k; F^\delta_j\cdot F^\delta_k\subseteq F^\delta_{\min(j,k)}, so each F^\delta_k is an ideal of Z; and 1\in F^\delta_k if and only if k\ge\max_\lambda\delta(\lambda). So if \delta>0 somewhere, F^\delta is not a unital algebra filtration.
  2. (Transport by \#.) \#(F^\delta_k)=F^{\delta\circ t}_k, where t(\lambda)=\lambda'. For the GB-depth this reads \#(F^a_k)=F^{n}_k. For n\ge2 the GB-depth filtration is not \#-stable: F^a_0=Ke_{(1^n)} and \#(F^a_0)=Ke_{(n)}. A depth \delta gives a \#-stable filtration if and only if \delta(\lambda')=\delta(\lambda) for all \lambda; examples are the symmetrised depth a(\lambda)+a(\lambda') and the max-hook depth \lambda_1+\lambda'_1-1.
  3. (Eigenvectors.) e_\lambda is \#-fixed if and only if \lambda=\lambda'. For \lambda\ne\lambda', e_\lambda+e_{\lambda'} and e_\lambda-e_{\lambda'} are (+1)- and (-1)-eigenvectors. If \operatorname{char}K\ne2, then Z=Z^+\oplus Z^- with \dim Z^\pm=\tfrac12\bigl(p(n)\pm sc(n)\bigr), where sc(n) is the number of self-conjugate partitions of n. (This dimension count follows directly by counting the +1 and -1 eigenvectors listed above.)
  4. (Conditional parity transfer.) Let P be a K-vector space with a linear involution \iota and projections \pi_d, let \Phi:Z\to P be linear, and assume \operatorname{char}K\ne2 together with the hypotheses (H-match) \Phi\circ\#=\iota\circ\Phi and (H-parity) \pi_d\circ\iota=(-1)^d\pi_d. Then \pi_d\Phi(e_\lambda)=0 for odd d when \lambda=\lambda'; \pi_d\Phi(e_{\lambda'})=(-1)^d\pi_d\Phi(e_\lambda) for all \lambda; and for odd d, \pi_d\Phi(e_\lambda)\ne0 if and only if \pi_d\Phi(e_\lambda)\ne\pi_d\Phi(e_{\lambda'}).

Item 4 does not depend on the depth filtration at all: it is a statement about the idempotents e_\lambda. Neither (H-match) nor (H-parity) is established in the corpus. Item 2 shows that the GB-depth filtration and the transposition \lambda\mapsto\lambda' are not compatible, so the parity picture cannot be phrased as "\# preserves GB-depth".

The statistic \lambda_1+\lambda'_1-1 (the maximal hook length of \lambda) is referred to here as the max-hook depth, distinguishing it from Lusztig's a-function a(\lambda).
prf:cellular-depth-filtration:
Proof Proof of the cell-depth filtration properties. The a-function value. That the two-sided cell of shape \lambda has a-value \sum_i\binom{\lambda_i}2 (with (n) the index representation) is the type-A case of Lusztig's a-function, with each two-sided cell carrying exactly one irreducible [Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979]. It was checked exactly for n\le5 by computing the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis, the cells and a from the structure constants (probe recorded on issue #8094). Writing \binom{\lambda_i}{2}=0+1+\dots+(\lambda_i-1), a(\lambda) is the sum over cells (i,j) of \lambda of the column index j, and n(\lambda) is the sum of the row index i. Transposition swaps i and j, so a(\lambda')=n(\lambda).

Item 1. The e_\lambda are orthogonal idempotents, e_\lambda e_\mu=\delta_{\lambda\mu}e_\lambda, so a product of two generators of F_j and F_k is either 0 or a generator e_\lambda with \delta(\lambda)\le\min(j,k). Bilinearity gives F_jF_k\subseteq F_{\min(j,k)}. If 1\in F_k and \delta(\mu)>k, then e_\mu annihilates every generator of F_k, hence e_\mu=e_\mu\cdot1=0, a contradiction; conversely 1=\sum_\lambda e_\lambda.

Item 2. \# is an algebra automorphism sending each generator e_\lambda of F^\delta_k to e_{\lambda'}, and \delta(\lambda)=(\delta\circ t)(\lambda')\le k. So \#(F^\delta_k)\subseteq F^{\delta\circ t}_k, and applying \# again (it is an involution and t\circ t=\mathrm{id}) gives equality. With \delta=a, a\circ t=n. For n\ge2, the only partition with a(\lambda)=0 is (1^n) and \#(e_{(1^n)})=e_{(n)} with a((n))=\binom n2>0. Stability holds if and only if every level set of \delta is closed under t, which is \delta\circ t=\delta. The max-hook depth is transpose-invariant because the hook of (i,j) in \lambda' equals the hook of (j,i) in \lambda.

Item 3. Orthogonal nonzero idempotents are distinct, so e_{\lambda'}=e_\lambda if and only if \lambda'=\lambda. The eigenvector statements follow from \#(e_\lambda)=e_{\lambda'} and \#^2=\mathrm{id}. The dimension count uses linear algebra on the basis \{e_\lambda\}.

Item 4. (a) For \lambda=\lambda', \iota\Phi(e_\lambda)=\Phi(\#e_\lambda)=\Phi(e_\lambda), so for odd d, \pi_d\Phi(e_\lambda)=\pi_d\iota\Phi(e_\lambda)=-\pi_d\Phi(e_\lambda), which is 0 since 2 is invertible. (b) \pi_d\Phi(e_{\lambda'})=\pi_d\iota\Phi(e_\lambda)=(-1)^d\pi_d\Phi(e_\lambda). (c) For odd d and x=\pi_d\Phi(e_\lambda), (b) gives \pi_d\Phi(e_{\lambda'})=-x, and x\ne-x if and only if x\ne0.

The identity \#(e_\lambda)=e_{\lambda'} used in items 2–4 is taken from [Mathas 1999, Ch. 3] and [Dipper–James 1986]; given it, items 1–4 hold for any commutative algebra Z with orthogonal idempotents e:\iota\to Z. \blacksquare
def:hecke-curvature-2-cocycle:
Definition Hecke curvature 2-cocycle F. The Hecke curvature 2-cocycle is the 2-form-valued bilinear map F \in C^2(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)) defined on generator pairs by the deviation from Hecke and Yang-Baxter flat relations:

  F(\sigma_i, \sigma_j) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    R_H(i) & \text{if } i = j, \\
    R_{YB}(i) & \text{if } |i - j| = 1, \\
    [\sigma_i, \sigma_j] & \text{if } |i - j| \geq 2.
  \end{cases}

It extends to general elements via the Leibniz rule.
rem:hecke-curvature-2-cocycle-remark: Remark The Hecke curvature 2-cocycle as a flatness defect. The Hecke curvature 2-cocycle measures the failure of commutativity and normal-form flatness at each generator pair.
def:curvature-rank: Definition Curvature-rank r(T_w). The curvature-rank r(T_w) is the smallest non-negative integer r mapping the r-fold iterated curvature F^{\,r}(T_w) into the J^{\,r}(q) \setminus J^{\,r+1}(q) filtration stratum.
rem:curvature-rank-remark: Remark Curvature-rank as a reduction count. The curvature-rank counts the minimal number of reduction steps required to drive T_w into normal form.
conj:curvature-rank-gb-stratification:
Conjecture Curvature-rank stratification of the GB filtration. The curvature-rank stratifies the GB filtration:

  J^{\,r}(q) / J^{\,r+1}(q)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\{T_w \in H_n(R, q)\ \bigm|\ r(T_w) = r\bigr\}.

The non-abelian Stokes residue of the Markov trace at depth \ell isolates the contribution from words of curvature-rank \ell.

rem:curvature-rank-gb-stratification-int: Remark Geometric reading: curvature-rank strata as Seifert-surface blow-up loci. Under the archimedean realization, the Markov trace acts as a boundary holonomy on a Seifert surface. The curvature 2-cocycle behaves as the curvature 2-form of the Frobenius-Hopf flat connection. The total mass decomposes via non-abelian Stokes into independent stratum integrals, each evaluating the curvature-rank components directly over the blow-up loci.
conj:quantum-dilogarithm-stratified:
Conjecture Quantum dilogarithm stratifies by partition GB-depth. Let A = H_n(R, q) be a semisimple Hecke algebra. Decompose its centre Z(A) by GB-depth of partitions. The analytic quantum dilogarithm admits a centre-stratified expansion:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr) = \sum_{k = 0}^{\infty} \bigl\langle \phi_q^{(k)}(z_i),\, T_w \bigr\rangle,

where the depth-k coefficient \phi_q^{(k)} is the Frobenius dual of the truncation increment. The partial sum \Phi_q^{[\leq k]} captures exactly the \bigoplus_{j \leq k} Z^{(j)}(A)-content.

Consequence (truncation), if the conjecture holds. For T_w with NF support depth k_\star(T_w), the trace truncates precisely to:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr) = \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i) \cdot T_w\bigr).

If the conjecture holds, the analytic infinite product truncates to a finite product as a Frobenius-paired identity, with truncation depth fixed by the NF support of T_w. What is proved is weaker: the depth strata of Z(A) are mutually orthogonal under the Frobenius pairing (partial argument, Step 1).
conj:two-filtration-bridge:
Conjecture Two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth \leftrightarrow partition-cellular GB-depth via e_\lambda. The substrate convolution Hopf algebra \mathcal{H}_q carries two distinct filtrations:

  • the iterated-integral depth on grouplikes, G^{(0)} \subseteq G^{(1)} \subseteq \cdots with G^{(n)} generated by \{\exp_q, \log_q, \mathrm{Li}_2^q, \ldots, \mathrm{Li}_n^q\};
  • the partition max-hook filtration on the centre Z(H_n(q)), Z^{(0)}(A) \subseteq Z^{(1)}(A) \subseteq \cdots generated by the central idempotents e_\lambda with \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) := \max_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square) (a partition-level filtration distinct from the word-level curvature-rank filtration of curvature-rank GB stratification used in stratified \Phi_q; identifying word rewrite depth with partition hook length remains unestablished).

Terminology. The statistic \max_\square h(\square) = \lambda_1+\lambda'_1-1 used in this block is now called the max-hook depth. The corpus fixes "GB-depth" to mean Lusztig's a-function a(\lambda)=\sum_i\binom{\lambda_i}{2}; see Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)), which also shows that either choice gives a filtration of Z(H_n(q)) by ideals, not a unital algebra filtration. Below, \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}} should be read as the max-hook depth.

These are different numbers — for the figure-8 self-conjugate cell \lambda = (2, 2), iterated-integral depth = 2 but partition GB-depth = 3 (max hook length). The conjecture: they are related, and the bridge is via the central primitive idempotents e_\lambda.
conj:two-filtration-bridge-general:
Conjecture Two-filtration bridge map in full generality: bar-class determines iterated-integral depth (self-conj \to 2, chiral pair \to 3) for all partitions. This conjecture extends the bridge map d_{\mathrm{II}} to all partitions of any n. It is conditional: it rests on Two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth \leftrightarrow partition-cellular GB-depth via e_\lambda, which defines d_{\mathrm{II}}, and on an unproved matching of the transposing involution \# on H_n(q) with orientation reversal on periods. The bar involution itself fixes every e_\lambda and does not separate \lambda from \lambda'.

What is proved. Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)), item 4, is the provable core: under two named hypotheses (H-match: \# is intertwined with orientation reversal by a realisation map \Phi; H-parity: orientation reversal acts on depth-d periods by (-1)^d), odd-depth components vanish on self-conjugate cells and are antisymmetric under \lambda\leftrightarrow\lambda'. It does not give the values 2 and 3, which need a further non-vanishing. Note also that the "otherwise" branch of the definition of d_{\mathrm{II}} in Two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth \leftrightarrow partition-cellular GB-depth via e_\lambda is empty, since every partition is either self-conjugate or half of the pair \{\lambda,\lambda'\}. So the boxed formula below restates that definition; the content of this conjecture is the existence of a realisation for which it is non-degenerate.
def:hq-bi-filtration:
Definition Knot-indexed bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} on the substrate convolution algebra. Let \mathcal{H}_q be the substrate convolution Hopf algebra (Frobenius–Hopf substrate), filtered by iterated-integral depth G^{(0)} \subseteq G^{(1)} \subseteq \cdots. For each Bring-embeddable knot/link K (Bring-embeddable knots) with dominant cell \lambda_K \vdash n_K and central primitive idempotent e_{\lambda_K} \in Z(H_{n_K}(q)) (explicit central idempotent), the knot-K-localised depth-n stratum is

  \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}
  \;:=\;
  \bigl\{\, \alpha \;\in\; G^{(n)}(\mathcal{H}_q)
        \;:\; e_{\lambda_K} \cdot \alpha \cdot e_{\lambda_K} = \alpha \,\bigr\}.

The double-indexed family \{\mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}\}_{n \geq 0,\;K} is the bi-filtration: a horizontal axis of iterated-integral depth n (Goncharov side) and a vertical axis of knot/braid class K (Hecke cell side).
conj:bring-trilog-depth-3-witness:
Conjecture Bring trilog at \zeta_5 as depth-3 grouplike value (50-digit functional-equation cross-validated witness). The depth-3 grouplike of \mathcal{H}_q at the primitive 5th root of unity \zeta_5 maps under archimedean realisation to a class in \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2:

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\,\mathrm{Li}_3^q(\zeta_5)\,\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)
  \;+\;
  i\,S_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)
  \;\in\;
  \mathcal{P}_3 \big/ \mathcal{P}_2.

The canonical evaluation verifies this equivalence to 50 decimal places. The Bring-orbit functional equation confirms the sum identically without relying on specific polylogarithm implementations, supplying a strict 50-digit cross-validation.

The algebraic depth matches the Goncharov period depth. The specific geometric realization remains open, though hyperbolic 4-manifold volumes on Bring-cusped quotients constitute the primary candidate. This constitutes the first depth-3 canonical witness, subjecting the graded-Mikusiński correspondence to falsifiability tests at depths 2 and 3.
conj:joint-galois-braid-action:
Conjecture Joint motivic-Galois \times braid-group action on the bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}. Let \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} be the knot-indexed bi-filtration (Knot-indexed bi-filtration \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} on the substrate convolution algebra). Two groups act on it by symmetry:

  • the motivic Galois group G_{\mathrm{mot}} acts on the depth axis, permuting Goncharov period classes \mathcal{P}_n / \mathcal{P}_{n-1} under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} (Kontsevich–Zagier 2001, Goncharov 2001);
  • the braid group B_{n_K} acts on the knot axis, permuting Wedderburn cells e_{\lambda_K} via the standard representation on H_{n_K}(q).

Conjectural joint structure: these two actions extend to a joint action of a semi-direct product G_{\mathrm{mot}} \rtimes B_{n_K} on \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)}, with the action on each axis being equivariant with respect to the action on the other:

  \boxed{\;
    g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta \cdot \alpha)
    \;=\;
    \beta \cdot g_{\mathrm{mot}}(\alpha)
    \quad\text{for } \alpha \in \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)},\;
    g_{\mathrm{mot}} \in G_{\mathrm{mot}},\;
    \beta \in B_{n_K}.
  \;}

Equivalently: the motivic-Galois action commutes with the braid- group action when restricted to the bi-filtration, and the joint group G_{\mathrm{mot}} \times B_{n_K} stabilises each \mathcal{H}_q^{(n, K)} stratum.
def:adelic-substrate:
Definition Adelic substrate \mathbb{A}. The adelic substrate of the QOU framework is the ring of adeles of \mathbb{Q},

  \mathbb{A}
  \;=\;
  \mathbb{R} \;\times\; \prod_{p}{}^{\!\!\prime}\;\mathbb{Q}_p,

the restricted product of the archimedean completion \mathbb{R} with all p-adic completions \mathbb{Q}_p (restriction: almost all components lie in the maximal compact subring \mathbb{Z}_p).
def:archimedean-realization-functor:
Definition Archimedean realization functor \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}. The archimedean realization functor \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} is the composite

  \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}
  \;:\;
  \widehat{\mathcal{M}}
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\;\chi_{\mathrm{top}}\;\;}\;
  \widehat{\mathcal{M}} \otimes_{K_0(\mathrm{Var})} \mathbb{Z}
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\;\pi_\infty\;\;}\;
  \mathbb{R}

sending the motivic class [X] to its topological Euler characteristic \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(X) followed by the archimedean projection \pi_\infty \colon \mathbb{A} \to \mathbb{R}.
rem:archimedean-realization-functor-inte:
Remark Archimedean realization: functor vs. motivic measure and identification with \tau. Realization and projection. A motivic integral \int_{\mathcal{L}(X)} d\mu \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} defines a geometric shape. The topological realization \chi_{\mathrm{top}} maps this shape to an integer (Euler characteristic) or a refined Hodge-theoretic invariant like hyperbolic volume. The adelic projection \pi_\infty discards non-archimedean components, returning the real-valued laboratory measurement.

Level of the construction (functor vs. motivic measure). As written, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} has domain the Grothendieck ring \widehat{\mathcal{M}} = K_0(\mathrm{Var})^{\wedge}, and \chi_{\mathrm{top}} \colon K_0(\mathrm{Var}) \to \mathbb{Z} is a ring homomorphism — a motivic measure in the sense of Denef–Loeser — while \pi_\infty is an archimedean place. A map out of a ring is not a functor between categories: "functor" is literally accurate only for the fibre functor \tau (below), or when the domain is lifted to the category of motives \mathrm{DM}(k), where Betti/Hodge realization is a bona fide functor. On \widehat{\mathcal{M}} itself, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} is the archimedean realization / evaluation into \mathbb{R}, not a functor between QOU categories — consistent with the notation register, which reserves "functor" for \tau and treats the R \mapsto \mathbb{R} realization as an evaluation. The block label is retained for stability.

Identification with the fibre functor. The QOU fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Arch} is the exclusive exit from the categorical substrate to the real numbers. On motivic QOU inputs, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} coincides exactly with the archimedean component of \tau:

  \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}
  \;=\;
  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}
  \;:=\;
  \pi_\infty \circ \tau
  \quad\text{on } \widehat{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{QOU}}
  \;\subseteq\; \widehat{\mathcal{M}}.

Synthesis. The framework processes discrete categorical data along a single chain: adelic stitching, motivic integration, and archimedean projection. It requires no continuous differential equations or Lebesgue measures. The Kashaev limit of the algebraic quantum volume exemplifies this mechanism.
prop:archimedean-functor-uniqueness:
Proposition Uniqueness of the archimedean realization functor (Bloch-Suslin pentagon, conditional). Conditional on (1{-}q)\,\log\Phi_n(x; q) \to \mathrm{Li}_2(x) under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} and on the Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness theorem [suslin1991]. Let \tau_{\text{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau be the archimedean realization functor of the QOU substrate (archimedean realization functor), acting on motivic inputs assembled from braid / knot data. Under hypotheses (C1)–(C2) below, \tau_{\text{arch}} is uniquely determined, up to a single multiplicative real scalar, by the requirement that

  \lim_{q \to 1}\;\tau_{\text{arch}}\bigl(\Phi_q(z)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  D(z)
  \;:=\;
  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \log|z|\,\arg(1-z)

equal the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm on every shape parameter z \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\}, where:

  • (C1) The substrate's mass-formula state sum is pentagon-coherent: \tau_{\text{arch}} is a continuous, antisymmetric, real-valued functional on B(\mathbb{C}) — the structural content provided by the cosimplicial / Yekutieli triple machinery (Cosimplicial crossed groupoid) together with the archimedean limit assumed in the opening banner.
  • (C2) Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness [suslin1991, bloch2000]: any continuous antisymmetric pentagon-coherent real-valued function on \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\} is a constant scalar multiple of the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm D.

The uniqueness reduces to the Bloch-Suslin pentagon characterisation: D is the unique (up to a real scalar) continuous, antisymmetric, real-valued function on \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\} satisfying the 5-term pentagon identity

  D(x) - D(y) + D\!\left(\tfrac{y}{x}\right)
  - D\!\left(\tfrac{1-y^{-1}}{1-x^{-1}}\right)
  + D\!\left(\tfrac{1-y}{1-x}\right) \;=\; 0.

Theorem (conditional on (1{-}q)\,\log\Phi_n(x; q) \to \mathrm{Li}_2(x) under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}). The upstream archimedean-limit conjecture is taken as a hypothesis, and the Bloch-Suslin pentagon-uniqueness theorem [suslin1991, bloch2000] is likewise taken as a hypothesis (cited, not re-proved). The uniqueness statement is proved from these two hypotheses alone, and therefore qualifies as a rigorous conditional result rather than an unproved conjecture.

rem:adelic-substrate-integration:
Remark Motivation for the adelic substrate and Tate integration. Each non-archimedean place p corresponds to a localized quantum geometric state of the substrate: a specific q-deformation evaluated at a primitive root of unity, equivalently a Kummer level in the Habiro / cyclotomic completion (algebraic quantum volume). The archimedean place \infty — the \mathbb{R} component — is the laboratory continuum.

Motivation for the adelic substrate. Replacing \mathbb{R} by \mathbb{A} resolves a structural tension: the local q-geometries at each prime do not assemble into a continuous manifold, but they do assemble into a global adelic object. The macroscopic universe is therefore not the real continuum \mathbb{R} alone but the simultaneous integration of all local non-archimedean data weighted by their archimedean shadow.

Adelic integration (Tate's thesis). Global observables of the substrate — the macroscopic mass functional, the global L-function of Bring's coordinate ring, the partition functions of the brane tower — are not Riemann integrals over \mathbb{R}. They are Tate integrals over \mathbb{A}:

  \mathcal{Z}(s)
  \;=\;
  \int_{\mathbb{A}^\times} \! f(x)\,|x|^s\, d^\times x
  \;=\;
  \zeta_\infty(s) \cdot \prod_{p} \zeta_p(s),

a product of local zeta integrals, one per place. The classical \zeta(s) is recovered as the global Tate integral of the standard adelic Schwartz function. Local q-zeta data and macroscopic real-valued observables are two faces of the same adelic object.

Discrete quantum data at every prime is glued by adelic restriction and projected to physical numbers by the archimedean realization functor.
rem:motivic-substrate-canonicity:
Remark Canonicity, realizations, and scope of the motivic substrate. Canonicity of the substrate. Three observations factor through \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}} rather than any single realization:

  • Mass formulas. The topological mass of a knot (motivic mass measure) is a class \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta) \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}}, not a real number. The real-valued mass arises only after applying \rho_\infty.
  • Adelic factorisation. The global zeta integral \mathcal{Z}(s) of the adelic substrate factorises as a restricted product \prod_v \zeta_v(s). This is the realization-tower factorisation \rho_{\mathrm{tot}} = \prod_v \rho_v applied to a single motivic class.
  • Habiro evaluation. The Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} is the universal target of the non-archimedean realizations of \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}}. The functor \rho_p evaluates a motivic class at the level-p root of unity. The inverse limit over p recovers the Habiro completion.

Every algebraic invariant taking values in \mathbb{R}, \mathbb{Q}_p, or the Habiro ring is the realization at some place v of a single motivic class living in \widehat{\mathcal{M}}.

Relation to existing blocks.

  • The Frobenius–Hopf substrate is the algebraic-place realization. It forms a finite-type structure on \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mot}}.
  • The arc space \mathcal{L}(X) provides the measurable space for motivic integration into \widehat{\mathcal{M}}. One derives the Kontsevich–Denef–Loeser motivic measure [kontsevich1995, denef-loeser2001] from this space.

Out of scope. Mixed motives, Bloch–Kato exact sequences, and full motivic Galois groups are not axiomatized here. The realization tower is presented purely as the family \{\rho_v\} of place-indexed evaluations; the categorical relationships among the \rho_v remain implicit.
